messages.author: 1e00f9a7223abbc1
messages.subject: RStudio + INLA using Docker
parts:
Hi everyone,

I managed to create a Docker image containing RStudio + INLA package.
The RStudio is the server version, so it is used through a web browser (Similar interface compared to the standalone version).
I did this to avoid frequent issues as:
  • Different environments causes results mismatch.
  • Difficulties reproducing results.
  • Trying out a new version.
I believe having RStudio with INLA in a docker container helps solving those issues.

The docker images are hosted in Docker Hub, and there are two version:
Stable version
Testing version
built from the respective repository.

I also prepared a bash script (for Linux/Unix/MacOS) to help launching the RStudio server. It can be found in GitHub
git clone https://github.com/egonzalf/rstudio-inla.git
cd rstudio-inla
./run-rstudio.sh

You can run ./run-rstudio.sh --help for more options.

To get started with docker and how to install it, please visit:
https://www.docker.com/community-edition


Hope this will be useful to somebody.
Best regards,

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] RStudio + INLA using Docker
parts:
On Tuesday, May 29, 2018 at 6:59:19 PM UTC+3, Virgilio Gómez-Rubio wrote:
Hi Eduardo,

This looks an interesting tool. I am curious about setting a Docker image to compile the R-INLA package on different platforms. This will ease testing the R-INLA package on different OS and under different versions of R. Would this be feasible?

I'm no expert with Docker,but I would say it is possible to do it.
In Docker Hub there are plenty of OS minimal images (ubuntu, fedora, centos, debian, etc), to start with. Then you would just need the instructions to install the development tools and the software stack needed for R and/or INLA.

My docker image is based on https://hub.docker.com/r/rocker/rstudio-stable/ which uses Debian stretch with R 3.4.4
 

Best,

Virgilio

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] RStudio + INLA using Docker
parts:
Dear Virgillio,

I'm using Docker both to build and test several of my R packages and
to run standarised analyses on AWS machines. The nice thing is that
Docker offers a very specific environment, even when run on different
machines. You can use any OS for which a Docker image exists.

I've created https://hub.docker.com/r/inbobmk/rstable/ which has a
stable version R version with a stable collection of R packages.

Have a look at R-hub too: https://github.com/r-hub/rhub, It offers
several OS's (https://github.com/r-hub/rhub#listing-r-hub-platforms)

Best regards,

messages.author: 9869e52e9a4f7d9a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] RStudio + INLA using Docker
parts:
Hi all,

I've been using INLA on my Debian Stretch based for a year now, where I compiled INLA from source code, and it works amazingly well (and performs much faster as well since I compiled it from source). Here's the Makefile I've been using more recently: https://gist.github.com/sadatnfs/6b15bdc68b2224b19853121a9e1bfcbb

Note that this is using a fork from the original INLA repo, because of a small fix they haven't yet implemented in the Makefile for inlaprog (linking Pardiso). This build combined with R-3.5.0 built from source, GCC/G++ 8.1.0, and MKL linked BLAS/LAPACK is a beast indeed. Hopefully this helps somewhat!

Nafis
